reason: Verified in code and by driving. lately.html has exactly one instant, F.readingLong = "09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026" (fixture.js:27; the fixture carries readingDate and readingTime and nothing else time-shaped, so no prior-reading instant exists anywhere in the source). In state=error that one string is printed three times from three labels: shell() line 725 "Read at ...", shell() line 735 coverage "Read ...", and error() line 817 "Last good reading · ...". Driving lately.html?v=light&state=error and counting text nodes containing the fixture instant returns 3 for error against 2 for every other state, the third being "Last good reading · 09:14, Thursday 16 July 2026"; it is legible in shots/light-error--1440x960.png directly under "Try again". The card whose entire job is to say Tasks did not answer therefore asserts, in the same card, that a reading succeeded at the exact instant of the attempt that failed - a fact the surface does not hold. That is the honest-degradation contract's own defect class (a fabricated last-good-reading is a fabricated zero wearing a timestamp), committed on the protected state built to prevent it, so misleading is the right class, not defect. Not gate-restated: interaction-check.mjs:339-351 asserts only that the instant appears at least once per state (anchored >= 1), which this passes while still being false; the gate cannot see the label. Not already handled, no constraint touched, no colour or weight or architecture proposed. The problem stands. The proposed fix is directionally right but wrong in two of its three clauses, so it is corrected rather than adopted.
sharpenedFix: 1) Delete the "Last good reading" line from error() (line 817) outright rather than conditioning it. The lab fixture is bound to src/lib/project-truth-fixture.ts, which records no reading history at all, so there is no instant to print and no honest branch to write; a conditional the data can never satisfy is dead code that reads as a promise. If a stale reading is ever to be shown it needs its own bound field (a lastGoodReading in derive-fixture.mjs, joined to the bound list, never to labAuthored - a lab-authored staleness stamp would be the same fabrication with a footnote). 2) Do not ship "Nothing has been read today." It swaps one unheld fact for another: the surface has no day-scoped read history either, and "today" is a scope this twelve-week look-back never uses. If a line is wanted where the stamp was, say what is actually known - that the retry is the only way forward - or leave the space empty; the card already carries "Try again". 3) Do not drop the header line alone. The header's "Read at" (725) and the coverage strip's "Read" (735) print the same string under the same verb; removing one and leaving the other keeps the identical claim on screen while breaking the header rule, whose flex rule and "Twelve weeks" chip would be left orphaned (that rule is already fragile at 390 - see reading-rule-dangles-at-390). Treat the pair as one decision: either both keep the instant as the moment the surface was resolved, or both change verb together to an attempt wording. This finding's fabrication is the "Last good" label, and clause 1 alone removes it.
breaks: Deleting the stamp changes the error card's vertical rhythm - the .center stack loses its last child, so the card's height and the optical centring of "Try again" both move; re-measure the error frame at 1440/1280/768/390 in both grounds and re-shoot light-error and dark-error at all four widths. If clause 3 is ever taken further and the instant is removed from error entirely, interaction-check.mjs:339-351 fails on state=error (anchored drops to 0 against its >= 1 assertion) and either the coverage strip must keep a labelled instant or that loop's state list must be amended deliberately, not silently. Re-run both gates after the edit: audit.mjs for the type ramp, leading and AA contrast of the remaining .t-label dim text against the real composited card, and interaction-check.mjs in full for the unanchored-time block and the zero-console-errors assertion. console.html (1049) and surface.html (972) carry byte-identical copies of the same line and will drift out of sync unless edited in the same pass.
